correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary prime-power q, the Frobenius-reversal star is a genuine anti-involution on upper triangular matrices over \(\mathbb F_{q^2}\). The palindromic diagonal condition is necessary. The star-unitriangular Hermitian factorization is proved by filtration and surjective \(\mathbb F_{q^2}\)/\(\mathbb F_q\) trace, including characteristic two. Explicit conjugator b=Ee+(1-E)(1-e) and factorization in the sparse star-stable centralizer prove unitary transitivity. Orbit–stabilizer gives \(q^{r(n-r)}\) per compatible diagonal; rank selection gives the formulas. A uniform \(O((1+h^2)/n)\) central-binomial-ratio bound and summable \(q^{-h^2}\) tail give total-variation \(O_q(1/n)\). The independent finite-field program directly enumerated and tested nine cases and printed VERIFY_OK. Finite tests are not treated as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The fixed idempotents correspond to orthogonal direct-summand projections compatible with a distinguished complete Hermitian flag, so their rank spectrum is a canonical structural invariant. Exact square-root fiber cardinalities contrast sharply with the established unrestricted \(q^{2r(n-r)}\) fibers and remain valid even in characteristic two. The new three residue-class discrete-Gaussian limits quantify nontrivial bounded rank fluctuations with explicit \(O_q(1/n)\) total-variation control. This is a natural infinite family and a nonroutine unitary orbit-count, not an arbitrary finite slice.
